subject: pathology
title: Emphysema: Centriacinar and Panacinar Patterns, Alpha-1 Antitrypsin, and Chronic Bronchitis

steps.tx: Emphysema destroys alveolar walls and elastic recoil without obvious fibrosis, enlarging airspaces permanently until the lung cannot empty, trapping air behind prematurely collapsing airways on expiration. Protease excess over antiprotease protection drives the destruction: **emphysema as protease-antiprotease imbalance**. Diffusing capacity falls as alveolar capillary surface disappears, distinguishing emphysema from chronic bronchitis where it stays better preserved.
steps.say: Emphysema is permanent airspace enlargement from wall destruction; recoil lost, air trapped, breathlessness follows.

steps.tx: Look at the two lobes in this specimen and compare how completely their airspaces have vanished. Upstairs, destruction hugs the bronchiole at the centre of each acinus, while downstairs every airspace in the acinus has opened into one wide cavity. That lower lobe pattern is **panacinar emphysema**, the form linked with alpha one antitrypsin deficiency. Upper lobe centriacinar disease instead follows smoke exposure, so the geography of loss already points towards its cause before any blood test returns.
steps.say: Centriacinar loss favours upper lobes in smokers, while panacinar loss clears whole lower lobe acini when antitrypsin is lacking.

steps.tx: Centriacinar emphysema attacks respiratory bronchioles at lobule centres of upper lobes in smokers, sparing distal alveoli initially, while panacinar disease erases whole acini uniformly in lower lobes. Distribution separates them: **centriacinar versus panacinar emphysema patterns**. Paraseptal emphysema, the third recognised pattern, lines pleura and fissures and predisposes younger patients to spontaneous pneumothorax.
steps.say: Smokers destroy lobule centres up top; alpha-1 deficiency erases whole acini down below.

steps.tx: Alpha-1 antitrypsin normally shields lung elastin from neutrophil elastase, and its severe Z allele deficiency leaves young lungs defenceless while misfolded protein simultaneously injures hepatocytes into cirrhosis. One protein, two organs: **alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency, lung and liver disease**. The PiZZ genotype carries the highest risk, and augmentation therapy uses pooled human alpha-1 protein in carefully selected PiZZ patients.
steps.say: Alpha-1 deficiency destroys young lungs for lack of protection and livers from trapped misfolded protein.

vis.caption: Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency emphysema patterns with panacinar lower lobe destruction.

steps.tx: Serum protein electrophoresis betrays alpha-1 deficiency through a shrunken alpha-1 globulin peak, prompting level and Pi genotype testing in early emphysema, family disease, or unexplained cirrhosis. The missing peak performs **alpha-1 antitrypsin screening on electrophoresis**. Testing suits anyone whose emphysema begins before age 45 years, shows basal predominance, or arrives alongside unexplained liver disease.
steps.say: A missing alpha-1 peak on electrophoresis should trigger level and genotype testing in young emphysema.

vis.caption: Serum electrophoresis patterns, where a reduced alpha-1 band betrays antitrypsin deficiency.

steps.tx: Chronic bronchitis is defined clinically, productive cough for three months in two successive years, produced by goblet cell hyperplasia and submucosal gland hypertrophy flooding airways with mucus. Its bedside definition needs no scanner: **chronic bronchitis, clinical definition**. The Reid index compares gland layer thickness with total bronchial wall thickness, and values above 0.5 mark submucosal gland hypertrophy.
steps.say: Three months of productive cough in two successive years defines chronic bronchitis clinically.

steps.tx: Pink puffers stay pink by hyperventilating through destroyed lungs, thin and barrel chested, while blue bloaters hypoventilate behind mucus, becoming cyanosed, carbon dioxide retaining, and right heart strained. Those poles remain **emphysema and bronchitis clinical phenotypes**. Cor pulmonale announces itself through raised jugular pressure, hepatic congestion, and ankle oedema once pulmonary pressures climb high enough.
steps.say: Pink and puffing versus blue and bloated: physiology paints the two COPD poles at the bedside.

rows: Pink, near normal gases until late

steps.tx: Smoking cessation is the only intervention proven to slow emphysema's forced expiratory decline toward normal ageing, making every consultation a cessation intervention beside inhalers and rehabilitation. That primacy defines **smoking cessation in obstructive lung disease**. Sustained quitting also cuts exacerbation frequency and lung cancer risk, benefits no inhaler regimen has matched in trials.
steps.say: Only quitting smoking bends the emphysema decline curve; inhalers ease symptoms beside that fact.

nodes.label: Smoking status asked at every visit

steps.tx: Bullae, giant emphysematous spaces, can rupture into pneumothorax or compress salvageable lung enough for surgical or bronchoscopic volume reduction in selected upper lobe disease. Selection governs **lung volume reduction in severe emphysema**. Patients whose forced expiratory volume and diffusing capacity both sit at or below 20 percent predicted face prohibitive operative risk.
steps.say: Giant bullae and upper lobe disease select the few who gain from volume reduction procedures.
